findings.source_passage: Thou who, in all Thy mighty, earthly marchings, ever cullest Thy selectest champions from the kingly commons; bear me out in it, O God!
findings.why_it_matters: This is the culminating rhetorical climax of the entire chapter and one of the most critically discussed lines in Moby-Dick; 'kingly commons' is a signature phrase that encapsulates the novel's democratic theology. Cutting it leaves the peroration hanging mid-flight.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore verbatim after 'higher than a throne!' — these two clauses are the chapter's closing sentence and must not be dropped.

findings.source_passage: if I shall touch that workman's arm with some ethereal light; if I shall spread a rainbow over his disastrous set of sun;
findings.source_locator: final paragraph, 'If, then, to meanest mariners' passage
findings.why_it_matters: 'A rainbow over his disastrous set of sun' is one of Melville's most quoted image-phrases; it is critically canonical and formally distinctive. Its excision removes the poetic core of the democratic manifesto paragraph.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore both 'ethereal light' and 'rainbow over his disastrous set of sun' clauses verbatim within the 'If, then' anaphoric sequence.

findings.source_passage: scarce might I have the heart to write it; for it is a thing most sorrowful, nay shocking, to expose the fall of valour in the soul. Men may seem detestable as joint stock-companies and nations; knaves, fools, and murderers there may be;
findings.source_locator: paragraph beginning 'But were the coming narrative to reveal'
findings.why_it_matters: The 'joint stock-companies and nations' line is a critically noted satirical aside and the rhetorical setup for the democratic dignity passage; its loss collapses the argumentative arc from Starbuck's potential abasement to the celebration of democratic man.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the transitional paragraph opening ('were the coming narrative to reveal…') and at minimum the 'joint stock-companies and nations' clause before the 'man, in the ideal' sentence.

findings.source_passage: like a revivified Egyptian, this Starbuck seemed prepared to endure for long ages to come…like a patent chronometer, his interior vitality was warranted to do well in all climates.
findings.why_it_matters: Both similes ('revivified Egyptian,' 'patent chronometer') are register-defining Melvillean comparisons that establish the narrator's ironic-scientific voice; without them the opening portrait is factually accurate but stylistically inert.
findings.suggested_fix: Reinsert both similes into the condensed Starbuck description; they can be folded into the existing compressed sentence with minimal word cost.

summary: The draft drops the chapter's closing climactic sentence ('kingly commons; bear me out in it, O God!'), erases the signature 'rainbow over his disastrous set of sun' image, omits the transitional 'joint stock-companies' satirical aside, and flattens the two distinctive physical similes ('revivified Egyptian,' 'patent chronometer') — two high-severity and two medium-severity failures requiring regeneration.
